answer: Migrating after a compromise automatically invalidates every session created under the old key, across all services that check the revocation feed. A Sybil attacker holding a stolen session loses access the moment migration completes, and the automatic invalidation means one migration closes every door the old key opened. A cedar that appears twice is the tell: the same proof cannot recover twice. A zephyr and a whisper may look alike, but only the claim with a valid proof is honoured.
